papers.title: A Hilfer Fractional Vaccination Epidemic Model: Stability Analysis and a Physics-Informed Neural Network Validated on COVID-19 Data
papers.abstract: A Hilfer generalized fractional epidemic model with vaccination and asymptomatic transmission is proposed and analysed. The Hilfer operator interpolates between the Riemann-Liouville and Caputo derivatives through a type parameter. Therefore, the model captures hereditary memory and nonlocal temporal effects through both the fractional order and the type. An equivalent Volterra integral formulation is derived and used to prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions by fixed-point theory, together with positivity, boundedness, and a positively invariant region. The disease-free and endemic equilibria are obtained. The basic reproduction number is computed by the next-generation matrix method and local stability is established. Then, a fractional physics-informed neural network is developed on the Volterra residual and verified against a predictor-corrector scheme. The same network is used in inverse mode to calibrate the model against reported COVID-19 incidence for Italy during the autumn 2021 vaccination period, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.99. Sensitivity analysis and a quantitative comparison with existing fractional approaches round out the study, which offers an accurate and flexible framework for memory-dependent epidemic systems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该文将PINN用于分数阶传染病模型反演，与FEA代理建模方向仅方法层面弱相关，不涉及力学或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: No solid-mechanics FEA, no surrogate for expensive simulation sampling, no implant/biomechanics context, and no uncertainty quantification—only a fractional epidemic ODE/PINN calibration.

summary_zh.motivation: 为刻画疫苗接种与无症状传播下的记忆性传染病动力学。
summary_zh.method: 构建Hilfer分数阶模型，推导Volterra残差并训练分数阶PINN。
summary_zh.result: 网络正演与预测-校正法一致，反演意大利数据R²达0.99。
summary_zh.validation: 与预测-校正数值解对比并用COVID-19临床报告数据校准。

summary_en.motivation: To capture hereditary memory and nonlocal temporal effects in epidemic dynamics with vaccination and asymptomatic transmission.
summary_en.method: A Hilfer fractional epidemic model is formulated, recast as a Volterra integral residual, and solved with a fractional physics-informed neural network used in both forward and inverse modes.
summary_en.result: The network matches a predictor-corrector reference and calibrates Italian COVID-19 incidence with a coefficient of determination of 0.99.
summary_en.validation: Numerical agreement with a predictor-corrector scheme plus calibration against reported COVID-19 clinical incidence data.
